message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can copy/paste into your terminal or script.  
It shows exactly what HTTP calls you need to hit **VirusTotal’s DNS** endpoints, filters out everything but *CNAME* record objects, and prints only their `id` fields.

> ⚠️ Replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with your real key (`secret123`).  

---

### 1️⃣ Get all DNS “objects” for the domain

```bash
curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/records \
     --header "x-apikey: secret123"
```

This returns JSON like:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "dns-record--abcd",
      "attributes": { ... },
      "relationships": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

---

### 2️⃣ Filter for CNAME records & output only the IDs

If you’re on Linux/macOS, use `jq`. On Windows you could pipe through PowerShell’s `ConvertFrom-Json`.

#### Bash + jq

```bash
curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/records \
     --header "x-apikey: secret123" |
   jq -r '.data[] | select(.attributes.type=="cname") | .id'
```

Output will look like:

```
dns-record--a12b34cd56ef78gh90ij
dns-record--k23l45mn67op89qr01st
...
```

Each line is one CNAME record ID – no other metadata.

---

### 3️⃣ One‑liner (if you prefer)

```bash
curl -s -H"x-apikey: secret123" "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/records" | jq -r '.data[]|select(.attributes.type=="cname").id'
```

That’s it! No extra parsing needed—just the raw identifiers.
